solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Writer of volume twenty-six needing editing (8)

indicatorNotes.needing editing: an edited text has its parts rearranged

blocks.note: the answer to 26 across, IRATE, rearranged

annotation.surface: A writer whose twenty-sixth volume still needs an editor's pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twenty-six' is not a number to write down but a cross-reference: it means the answer to 26 across, IRATE.
annotation.definitionFit: Named by example: the French author of Candide is one particular writer.

entries.clue: Like a planet that is framing sun rising in front (8)

indicatorNotes.framing: a frame goes round what it holds
indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising reads bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: what comes before goes inside the next piece

blocks.note: the van is the front of an army or procession
IE (that is) round SUN gives ISUNE, which rises to ENUSI

annotation.surface: An astronomer describing a planet whose orbit frames the rising sun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In front' looks like a position; it is really 'inside VAN'. The reversal applies to the whole of I(SUN)E before it goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective of place: the -ian ending turns the second planet's name into 'of or like' it.

entries.clue: Mantel, say, came first with good English (5)

blocks.note: led = came first, as in a race

annotation.surface: Hilary Mantel coming first with a good English novel, as at a prize-giving.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital M makes it look like the novelist Hilary Mantel; 'say' shows a mantel (mantelpiece) is one example of a ledge.
annotation.definitionFit: A mantel is a shelf above a fireplace, which is a kind of ledge.

entries.clue: Large ship having broadcast facility with transmitter (8,7)

blocks.note: a carrier transmits, e.g. a disease; 'with' adds it on

annotation.surface: A big ship fitted with broadcasting equipment and a radio transmitter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' reads as a piece of equipment, but here it means a knack, which is CRAFT.
annotation.definitionFit: An aircraft carrier is one of the largest warships afloat.

entries.clue: How old ironwork deteriorates is truly awful (7)

indicatorNotes.awful: an awful version is a badly mangled one

annotation.surface: A complaint that watching old ironwork decay is truly awful.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole descriptive phrase asking 'how', so the answer must be an adverb.
annotation.definitionFit: Iron decays by corroding to reddish oxide, so an adverb built on that decay answers 'how'.

entries.clue: Caught express naval transport (6)

annotation.surface: Someone caught taking an express boat run by the navy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Express' sits by 'transport' to suggest a fast service; it is the verb, to express, giving UTTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A cutter is a small fast vessel, often a ship's boat.

entries.clue: Misadventure not ruffling calm (15)

indicatorNotes.ruffling: ruffling messes up the letters' order

annotation.surface: A mishap that failed to disturb someone's composure.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'not' as a negative on 'ruffling'; it is in fact three letters of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Undemonstrative means showing little feeling, reserved and calm.

entries.clue: Group of monstrous sea urchins — bottom drawer’s contents? (9)

indicatorNotes.Group of: the answer is a group of letters taken from the next words

annotation.surface: Some horrible sea urchins found at the back of the bottom drawer.
annotation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is British for the store of linen and clothes a bride-to-be collects, like an American hope chest.
annotation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers for married life.

entries.clue: Assigning rank to crew member (6)

blocks.note: grading or ranking something, a verbal noun
in the Royal Navy, an ordinary seaman below officer rank

annotation.surface: An officer giving a rank to one of the crew.
annotation.walkthrough: Two plain senses: the act of grading, and a naval seaman below officer rank.
annotation.definitionFit: Rating is both the act of ranking and a naval seaman below officer rank.

entries.clue: Judge taking steer about court employee? (6)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about into a new order

annotation.surface: A judge guiding a member of the court staff.
annotation.walkthrough: With a judge in the surface, 'court' means a law court; the question mark signals the royal court, where the jester worked.
annotation.definitionFit: A jester was employed to entertain at a royal court.

entries.clue: Lowest point of North America? Earth almost (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: drop its last letter

annotation.surface: A geography quiz: where is North America's lowest point, and is it nearly on the ground?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' is part of the wordplay's cover: the definition stops at 'point'.
annotation.definitionFit: Astronomy's term for the point directly below an observer, used figuratively for the depths of anything.

entries.clue: Cricketer securing duck to end career? This can be moving (9)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure is to hold fast, so BAT holds O fast inside it
indicatorNotes.to end: 'to end' sends that piece to the end of the next

blocks.note: to career = to rush along, to speed
BAT (a batsman) round O (a duck, zero runs)

annotation.surface: A cricketer out for a duck, wondering if it is time to retire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb, not a working life. The definition is cryptic: a speedboat is something that moves fast, with a nod to 'moving' as touching.
annotation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a boat built to move at speed.

entries.clue: Strength one found in used flavouring (9)

indicatorNotes.found in: the first pieces are found inside the next

blocks.note: SPENT = used, split to take the insert

annotation.surface: One source of strength located in a spent flavouring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Used' reads as second-hand; it is SPENT, which opens up to take ARM and I.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: this mint is one of the commonest flavourings in gum and toothpaste.

entries.clue: Provide staff for protecting very good rock artist (5)

indicatorNotes.protecting: MAN wraps round SO to protect it

annotation.surface: Hiring security staff to protect a very good rock musician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock artist' suggests a guitarist; it is someone who works stone.
annotation.definitionFit: A mason shapes and carves stone.

entries.clue: An insect in the WC? How to keep one’s distance? (7)

blocks.note: loo = WC, a British word for toilet

annotation.surface: An insect buzzing about in the toilet, and how best to stay away from it.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the first half literally: 'a loo fly' is an insect in the WC. The pieces join in the order the answer reads, not the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance is behaving aloofly.

entries.clue: Upset finished project (9)

annotation.surface: Someone upset that their project is finished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as an emotion; it is the verb, to topple. 'Project' is the verb too, not a piece of work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of toppling, as a regime or government is toppled.

entries.clue: Gets up around noon and washes (6)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so RISES encircles N

annotation.surface: A late riser who gets up around midday and has a wash.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a lazy morning; 'noon' is only the abbreviation N.
annotation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash with clean water.

entries.clue: Sons always see acutely (8)

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is one

annotation.surface: Sons who always have sharp eyesight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' is a verb in the surface, but crosswords often use it for a diocese, and ELY is the favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: Acutely and severely both mean intensely, as of pain.

entries.clue: Military policeman cut down outside Washington (6)

indicatorNotes.outside: 'outside' means on the exterior, so REAP sits on the exterior of DC

blocks.note: to reap = to cut down a crop

annotation.surface: A military policeman shot down outside Washington.
annotation.walkthrough: A redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cover on their caps.
annotation.definitionFit: British military police wear red caps, hence the nickname.

entries.clue: Favour bringing umpire in for each (6)

indicatorNotes.bringing: to bring someone in is to include them, so PER brings REF within it
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means inside, placing REF inside PER

annotation.surface: Favouritism shown by bringing in an umpire for each match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Favour' is a verb here, not a kindness done.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to favour one option over another is to like it better.

entries.clue: Animated cow lacking sign of hesitation to butt in (7)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the word is lacking the named letters

blocks.note: Ermintrude, the cow in the British children's cartoon The Magic Roundabout
erm = a hesitating noise, removed from the front

annotation.surface: A cartoon cow who charges in without hesitating.
annotation.walkthrough: Ermintrude is the cow from The Magic Roundabout, a British children's TV cartoon; take away ERM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to butt in is to push in where one is not wanted.

entries.clue: Standstill with idiot stuck in drive, no learner (7)

indicatorNotes.stuck in: stuck in means lodged inside, so ASS is lodged inside
indicatorNotes.no: 'no learner' means without the learner, so the L is taken out

annotation.surface: Traffic at a standstill because an idiot learner got stuck in the drive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drive' reads as a driveway or a motoring lesson; it is the verb, to impel.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French word for a dead end, used for any deadlock.

entries.clue: Sexy and courageous, destroying hearts, ensnaring tons (6)

indicatorNotes.ensnaring: what is left snares T inside

blocks.note: HEROIC (courageous) without H (hearts, as in cards)

annotation.surface: Someone sexy and brave, breaking hearts and catching many admirers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hearts' is the card-suit abbreviation H, not romance; HEROIC loses it before T goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: Erotic means sexually arousing, sexy.

entries.clue: What’s ultimately in copter, gyro, turbojet, dynamo and mower (5)

annotation.definition: What’s ultimately in copter, gyro, turbojet, dynamo and mower

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: copter, gyro, turbojet, dynamo and mower

annotation.surface: A list of machines, asking what they all have inside them.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: each of these machines has a rotor inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part in all five machines.

entries.clue: Seaplane flying either side of key seafront area (9)

indicatorNotes.flying: the letters fly about into a new order
indicatorNotes.either side of: the rearranged letters sit on both sides of D

blocks.note: SEAPLANE rearranged, split round the key

annotation.surface: A seaplane flying along either side of a key stretch of seafront.
annotation.walkthrough: Key is a musical key, D here; the rearranged SEAPLANE splits to sit either side of it.
annotation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level walkway along the seafront.

entries.clue: Saying unhappy wise man never has succeeded (5)

indicatorNotes.never has: 'never' reads as 'neither has', so neither word has the S for succeeded

annotation.surface: A saying about a wise man who is unhappy because he never succeeded.
annotation.walkthrough: One S is dropped from each of two words: SAD and SAGE both lose it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an old saying or proverb.

entries.clue: Running late, sailors must grab eats (9)

indicatorNotes.must grab: to grab is to seize and hold, so TARS hold DINES inside

annotation.surface: Sailors behind schedule who must grab a bite to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eats' looks like a noun, a snack; it is the verb, giving DINES.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun for lateness; 'running late' works as a noun phrase for that state.

entries.clue: Angry with copyright infringer stealing page (5)

annotation.surface: An author angry with a pirate who stole pages of their work.
annotation.walkthrough: A copyright infringer is a pirate, as in pirated DVDs; the P for page is stolen from it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, a little stronger than angry: furious.

entries.clue: Runner perhaps of company division (6)

blocks.note: a ward is an electoral or hospital division

annotation.surface: An athlete, perhaps, of a company's division.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; a coward is one who runs away, with 'perhaps' flagging that.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: one who flees from danger is one kind of runner, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: Church measure unknown burial ground (8)

annotation.surface: A church measuring out an unknown burial ground.
annotation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; 'unknown' is Y, an algebra variable.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a large burial ground, often not beside a church.
